segs.text: זוהר לסעודת סוכה

שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ יוֹמָא טָבָא קַדִּישָׁא. שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ חַגָּא קַדִּישָׁא. שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ אוּשְׁפִּיזָא קַדִּישָׁא. אַנְתְּ הוּא מִקְרָא קוֹדֶשׁ. זַמִּין אַנְתְּ לְהַהוּא אֲתַר דְּאִקְרֵי קוֹדֶשׁ. לְאִתְעַטְּרָא בֵּיהּ וּלְאִשְׁתְּאֲבָא בֵּיהּ. וְתִתְקַדַּשׁ וְיִשְׁתַּכַּח בָּךְ חֶדְוָתָא. הָא אַנְתְּ שָׁאִיב מֵהַהוּא עֲמִיקָא דַעֲמִיקָתָא. דְּנַחֲלִין וּמַבּוּעִין נַפְקִין מִנֵּיהּ. הָא יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאִתְקְרוּן קוֹדֶשׁ מְקַבְּלִין לָךְ בְּאַנְפִּין נְהִירִין. בְּחֶדְוָתָא וּבְתֻשְׁבְּחָתָּא. מְזַמְּנִין לָךְ מְתַקְּנִין לָךְ סְעוּדָתָא יַקִּירָא. מְסַדְּרִין פָּתוֹרֵי מְתַקְּנֵי גַּרְמַיְהוּ בְּמָאנֵי יְקָר. חֲדָאן וּמְשַׁבְּחִין שְׁבָחָא לְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא:

חַגָּא דְסֻכּוֹת כַּמָּה חָבִיב אַנְתְּ וְיַקִּיר. אַף עַל גַּב דְּיַרְחָא דָא בַּכֶּסֶה וְלָא בְאִתְגַּלְיָא. הָא בָּךְ גְּלוּיָא אִיהוּ בְּחֶדְוָתָא דְסִיהָרָא. בָּךְ אִשְׁתְּלִימַת סִיהָרָא וְאִתְנְהָרַת מֵאִמָּא עִלָּאָה. וְקַיְמַת לְאַנְהָרָא לְתַתָּאֵי מִגּוֹ נְהוֹרָא דִלְעֵלָא:

בָּךְ קֻדְּשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא פָּרִישׂ גַּדְפוֹי עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל וַחֲדִי עִמְּהוֹן. בָּךְ אִתְעַר סִטְרָא דִימִינָא לְעֵלָּא. בְּגִין דְּיִתְקַשַּׁר בֵּיהּ סִיהֲרָא וְיִתְנְהִירוּ אַנְפָּהָא כִּדְקָא חָזֵי. בָּךְ יִשְׂרָאֵל נַפְקִין בְּסִימָנִין רְשִׁימִין מִגּוֹ מַלְכָּא קַדִּישָׁא בְּגִין דְאִנּוּן נַצְחִין דִּינָא. דְּהָא בָּךְ נַפְקֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּרְשִׁימוּ דְמַלְכָּא בְּתֻשְׁבַּחְתָּא דְהִלּוּלָא. עָאלִין בַּסֻּכּוֹת וְנַטְלֵי אֶתְרוֹג בִּשְׂמָאלָא. וְלוּלָב בִּימִינָא. וְהָא חָמָאן עִלָּאִין וְתַתָּאִין דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל רְשִׁימִין בִּרְשִׁימִין דְּמַלְכָּא קַדִּישָׁא. דְּהָא אִנּוּן נַטְלִי סִּמָנִי מְהֵימְנוּתָא חוֹתָמָא דְמַלְכָּא עִלָּאָה:

בָּךְ כְּתִיב בַּסֻּכֹּ֥ת תֵּשְׁב֖וּ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים. בְּגִין לְאִתְחֲזָאָה דְיִשְׂרָאֵל יַתְבֵי בְּרָזָא דִמְהֵימְנוּתָא בְּלָא דְחִילוּ כְּלָל. דְהָא מְקַטְרְגָא אִתְפְּרַשׁ מִנַּיְהוּ. וְכָל מִקַטְרְגִי עִלָּאֵי אַהְדָרַן רְחִימִין לְיִשְׂרָאֵל. בָּךְ יִנְדְעוּן עִלָּאִין וְתַתָּאִין וְאִסְתַּלַּק יְקָרָא דְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא עֵלָּא וְתַתָּא כִּדְקָא יָאוּת. וְכָל אוּכְלְסִין עִלָּאִין פָּתְחֵי וְאָמְרִי וּמִי֙ כְּעַמְּךָ֣ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל גּ֥וֹי אֶחָ֖ד בָּאָ֑רֶץ:

בָּךְ יַתְבִין יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּצִלָּא דִמְהֵימְנוּתָא. וּבְגִין דָּא אַחְסִינוּ חֵירוּ לְהוּ וְלִבְנַיְהוּ לְעָלְמִין. וּמִתְבָּרְכִין בִּרְכָתָא עִלָּאָה. בָּךְ אֲנָן יָתְבִין בְּצִלָא דִמְהֵימְנוּתָא. וּבְגִין דָּא שְׁכִינְתָּא פָּרְסָא גַדְפָהָא עֲלָנָא מִלְעֵלָּא. בָּךְ אֲנָן מְזַמְּנִין לְאוּשְׁפִּיזִין קַדִּישִׁין דְּאִנּוּן אַבְרָהָם וְיִצְחָק וְיַעֲקֹב וּמֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן וְיוֹסֵף וְדָוִד. וְאִלֵּין צַדִּיקַיָּא אוּשְׁפִּיזִין קַדִּישִׁין שַׁוְיָן מְדוֹרֵיהוֹן עִמָּנָא בְּגוֹ הַאי צִלָא דִמְהֵימְנוּתָא. וְאַבְרָהָם אַבָּא קַדִּישָׁא קָרֵי עֲלָן: אָ֗ז תִּתְעַנַּג֙ עַל־יְהֹוָ֔ה וְהִרְכַּבְתִּ֖יךָ עַל־במותי [בׇּ‍֣מֳתֵי] אָ֑רֶץ וְהַאֲכַלְתִּ֗יךָ נַחֲלַת֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֣ב אָבִ֔יךָ כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהֹוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃ וְיִצְחָק אַבָּא קַדִּישָׁא קָרֵי עֲלָן: גִּבּ֣וֹר בָּ֭אָרֶץ יִהְיֶ֣ה זַרְע֑וֹ דּ֖וֹר יְשָׁרִ֣ים יְבֹרָֽךְ׃ הוֹן־וָעֹ֥שֶׁר בְּבֵית֑וֹ וְ֝צִדְקָת֗וֹ עֹמֶ֥דֶת לָעַֽד׃ וְיַעֲקֹב אַבָּא קַדִּישָׁא קָרֵי עֲלָן: אָ֣ז יִבָּקַ֤ע כַּשַּׁ֙חַר֙ אוֹרֶ֔ךָ וַאֲרֻֽכָתְךָ֖ מְהֵרָ֣ה תִצְמָ֑ח: וּמֹשֶׁה רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא קַדִּישָׁא, וְאַהֲרֹן כַּהֲנָא רַבָּא קַדִּישָׁא, וְיוֹסֵף צַדִּיקָא קַדִּישָׁא, קָרוּ עֲלָן, וְנָחֲךָ֣ יְהֹוָה֮ תָּמִיד֒ וְהִשְׂבִּ֤יעַ בְּצַחְצָחוֹת֙ נַפְשֶׁ֔ךָ וְעַצְמֹתֶ֖יךָ יַחֲלִ֑יץ וְהָיִ֙יתָ֙ כְּגַ֣ן רָוֶ֔ה וּכְמוֹצָ֣א מַ֔יִם אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹֽא־יְכַזְּב֖וּ מֵימָֽיו׃ וּבָנ֤וּ מִמְּךָ֙ חׇרְב֣וֹת עוֹלָ֔ם מוֹסְדֵ֥י דוֹר־וָד֖וֹר תְּקוֹמֵ֑ם וְקֹרָ֤א לְךָ֙ גֹּדֵ֣ר פֶּ֔רֶץ מְשֹׁבֵ֥ב נְתִיב֖וֹת לָשָֽׁבֶת׃ וְדָוִד מַלְכָּא מְשִׁיחָא קַדִּישָׁא דְאִיהוּ אִתְפַּקָּד עַל כָּל זְיָינֵי עָלְמָא קָרֵי עֲלָן, כׇּל־כְּלִ֞י יוּצַ֤ר עָלַ֙יִךְ֙ לֹ֣א יִצְלָ֔ח וְכׇל־לָשׁ֛וֹן תָּקוּם־אִתָּ֥ךְ לַמִּשְׁפָּ֖ט תַּרְשִׁ֑יעִי זֹ֡את נַחֲלַת֩ עַבְדֵ֨י יְהֹוָ֧ה וְצִדְקָתָ֛ם מֵאִתִּ֖י נְאֻם־יְהֹוָֽה׃

חַגָּא דְסֻכּוֹת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה חָבִיב אַנְתְּ וְיַקִּיר. הָא בָּךְ עַבְדֵינָן מִצְוַת סֻכָּה דְאִיהִי רְמִיזָא לְאִמָּא עִלָּאָה. לְסַכְּכָא עֲלָנָא כְּאִמָּא עַל בְּנִין, וּבָךְ אֲנָן מְזַמְּנִין גַּבָּן שִׁבְעָה אוּשְׁפִּיזִין עִלָּאִין קַדִּישִׁין. דְּאִנּוּן לָקֳבֵל שִׁבְעָה סְפִירָאן. דְּהָא בְּגִין שִׁבְעָה סְפִירָאן אָמַר קְרָא, כִּ֣י בַסֻּכּ֗וֹת הוֹשַׁ֙בְתִּי֙ אֶת־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּהוֹצִיאִ֥י אוֹתָ֖ם מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם. בְּשִׁבְעֶה עֲנָנֵי כָבוֹד. סוּכָּה מְלֵאָה בְּאוֹת וָא"ו אִיהִי בְּרָזָא דִּתְרֵין שְׁמָהָן. תְּרֵין כְּרוּבִים דְּהֵם סֹכְכִ֤ים בְּכַנְפֵיהֶם֙ עַל־הַכַּפֹּ֔רֶת וּפְנֵיהֶ֖ם אִ֣ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֑יו. וְהָא כְתִיב וְסֻכָּ֛ה תִּֽהְיֶ֥ה לְצֵל־יוֹמָ֖ם, דִּסְכָךְ בָּעֵינָן. וּסְכָךְ אִתְעֲבִיד לְצֵל דְּאִתְמַר בֵּיהּ בְּצֵ֥ל שַׁ֝דַּ֗י יִתְלוֹנָֽן, וְלָאו בְּצֵל סֻכַּת הֶדְיוֹט דַאֲגִין עַל גּוּפָא מְשִּׁמְשָׁא. אֶלָּא צֵל לַאֲגָנָא עַל נִשְׁמָתָא. כְּדִכְתִיב בְּצִלּוֹ֙ חִמַּ֣דְתִּי וְיָשַׁ֔בְתִּי:

חַגָּא דְסֻכּוֹת כַּמָּה חָבִיב אַנְתְּ וְיַקִּיר. הָא בָּךְ עַבְדֵינָן מִצְוַת נְטִילַת לוּלָב דְּדָמֵי לְחוּט הַשִּׁדְרָה. דְבֵיהּ שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר נִעְנוּעִין דְּלוּלָב. וְאִנּוּן לָקֳבֵל שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר בִּרְכָאן דִּצְלוֹתָא. וְלָקֳבֵל שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר אַזְכָּרוֹת דְּמִזְמוֹר הָבוּ לַה' בְּנֵי אֵלִים. וְלָקֳבֵל שְׁמֹנָה עָשָׂר אַזְכָּרוֹת דְּקְרִיאַת שְׁמַע. וְנִעְנוּעַ לְשִׁית סִטְרִין בְּחֻשְׁבָּן ו' וּתְלָת נִעְנוּעִין לְכָל סִטְרָא אִנּוּן חַי. לוּלָב דָּא צַדִּיק נַטְלֵינָן בַּיָּמִין. הָא אִיהוּ כָּלִיל שִׁית מִינִין. דְּאִנּוּן תְּלָת הֲדַסִים גְּדֻלָּה גְּבוּרָה תִּפְאֶרֶת. דְּדַמְיָן לִתְלַת גַּוְנֵי דְעֵינָא. עוֹד תְּרֵין בַּדֵּי עֲרָבוֹת נֶצַח וְהוֹד דְּדַמְיָן לִתְרֵין שַׁפְוָן. וְלוּלָב דְּאִיהוּ יְסוֹד דּוֹמֶה לַשִּׁדְרָה דְּבֵיהּ קִיּוּם כָּל גַּרְמִין. וַעֲלֵיהּ אָמַר דָּוִד מַלְכָּא כׇּ֥ל עַצְמוֹתַ֨י ׀ תֹּאמַרְנָה֮ יְהֹוָ֗ה מִ֥י כָ֫מ֥וֹךָ. וְנַטְלֵינָן בִּשְׂמָאלָא אֶתְרוֹג מַלְכוּת דְּדָמֵי לְלִבָּא דְּבֵיהּ הִרְהוּרִין. וּבְגִין דָּא אֶתְרוֹג הַדּוֹמֶה לַלֵּב תְּקִינוּ לְמֶהֶוֵי בְּיַד שְׂמֹאל. אֲבָל לוּלָב בְּיַד יָמִין דְּאִיהוּ בְרָזָא דְחֶסֶד דְּרוֹעָא יְמִינָא:

חַגָּא דְסֻכּוֹת כַּמָּה חָבִיב אַנְתְּ וְיַקִּיר. בָּךְ נַפְקֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּסִימָנִין רְשִׁימִין מִבֵּי מַלְכָּא. אִלֵין אִנּוּן מִינֵי דַאֲחִידָן בִּשְׁמָא קַדִּישָׁא. אִלֵין אִנּוּן סִימָנִי מְהֵימְנוּתָא חוֹתָמָא דְמַלְכָּא עִלָּאָה. דְּעָלַיְיהוּ אִתְמָר כֹּ֚ל הַנִּקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֔י וְלִכְבוֹדִ֖י בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף־עֲשִׂיתִֽיו׃ כֹּ֚ל הַנִּקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֔י הַיְינוּ דִכְתִיב פְּרִ֨י עֵ֤ץ הָדָר֙. וְלִכְבוֹדִ֖י בְּרָאתִ֑יו הַיְינוּ כַּפֹּ֣ת תְּמָרִ֔ים. יְצַרְתִּ֖יו הַיְינוּ וַעֲנַ֥ף עֵץ־עָבֹ֖ת. אַף־עֲשִׂיתִֽיו הַיְינוּ וְעַרְבֵי־נָ֑חַל:

בָּךְ כְּתִיב וּלְקַחְתֶּ֨ם לָכֶ֜ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן, דָּא הוּא דְנָפַק רִאשׁוֹן לְנַטְלָא בְמַבּוּעוֹי דְּמַיִּין נְבִיעִין. וַאֲנָן בָּעֵינָן לְאַמְשָׁכָא לֵיהּ. דְּהָא יוֹם הַכִּפֻרִים אַפִּיק לְכֹלָּא לְחֵירוּ. וּבְהָאי יוֹמָא מַטְרוֹנִיתָא עִלָּאָה דְּאִיהִי יוֹבְלָא דְּאַפִּיק לָן לְחֵירוּ אַעְטְרַת לְמַלְכָּא בְעִטְרוֹי, וְיַדְעֵינָן דְהָא מַיִּין נְבִיעִין עִמָּה שַׁרְיָין וְשָׁאִילְנָא לְמִשְׁתְּיָיא וְעַל דָּא קָרֵינָן לֵיהּ יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן:

וְעוֹד וּלְקַחְתֶּ֨ם לָכֶ֜ם בַּיּ֣וֹם הָרִאשׁ֗וֹן. דִּבְהָאי יוֹמָא אַבְרָהָם שֵׁירוּתָא דְכֹלָּא. אִי בַּעֲנָנִי יְקָר הוּא שֵׁירוּתָא. אִי בְּמַיָּיא הוּא שֵׁירוּתָא. דְּאַבְרָהָם שָׁרִי לְמֶחְפָּר בֵּירֵי דְמַיָּיא. פְּרִ֨י עֵ֤ץ הָדָר֙ דָּא בֵּירָא דְיִצְחָק. דְּיִצְחָק אַהְדַר לֵיהּ לְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וְקָרָא לֵיהּ הָדָר, פְּרִי דְּהָאי עֵץ הָדָר. כַּפֹּ֣ת תְּמָרִ֔ים דִּכְתִיב צַ֭דִּיק כַּתָּמָ֣ר יִפְרָ֑ח. וְלָא אִשְׁתַּכַּח בֵּינַיְיהוּ פֵּירוּדָא. וְעַל דָא לָא כְּתִיב וְכַפֹּת אֶלָא כַּפֹּת. בְּגִין דְּלָא סָלִיק בְּלָא דָא. וּבְהָאי אִתְמַלְיָיא הָאי בְּאֵר מִבְּאֵר מַיִם עִלָּאִין נְבִיעִין. הוּא אִתְמְלֵי בְּקַדְמִיתָא וּמִנֵּיהּ אִתְמַלְיָא בֵּירָא עַד דְאִיהוּ נְבִיעוּ לְכֹלָּא. וַעֲנַ֥ף עֵץ־עָבֹ֖ת דָּא עַנְפָא דְּאִילָנָא רַבְרְבָא. דְּאַתְקִיף וְאִשְׁתָּרְשָׁא בְּשָׁרְשׁוֹי, אִתְעֲבִיד אִילָנָא עִלָּאָה עַל כֹּלָּא דְּאַחִיד בְּכָל סִטְרִין עֲנַף דְּאִיהוּ עֵץ עָבֹת. עֵץ דְּאַחִיד לְאָבוֹת. דְּהָא מֵהָאי נָטַל יְסוֹדָא דְעָלְמָא וְאִתְמַלְיָא לַאֲרָקָא בְּבֵירָא. הָאי הוּא עָלְמָא אַרְקָא דְשַׁקְיוּתָא. וְעַרְבֵי־נָ֑חַל תְּרֵי אִנּוּן. תְּרֵין נַחֲלִין דְּמַיָּא אִתְכְּנִישׁ בְּהוּ לַאֲרָקָא לְצַדִּיק:

חַגָּא דְסֻכּוֹת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה חָבִיב אַנְתְּ וְיַקִּיר. בָּךְ כְּתִיב בַּסֻּכֹּ֥ת תֵּשְׁב֖וּ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים, דָּא הוּא רָזָא דִּמְהֵימְנוּתָא. שִׁבְעַת יָמִים מֵעָלְמָא עִלָּאָה לְתַתָּאָה. דְּכֻלְהוּ קָיְימֵי בְקִיּוּמָא לְאַנְהָרָא לְהָאי סֻכּוֹת. דְּאִיהִי סֻכַּת דָּוִד סֻכַּת שָׁלוֹם. וְעַמָּא קַדִּישָׁא יָתְבֵי תְּחוֹת צִלָּהָא בְּרָזָא דִמְהֵימְנוּתָא. וְהָא מָאן דְּיָתִיב בְּצִלָא דָא יָתִיב בְּאִנּוּן יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין. וְעַל דָא אַף עַל גַּב דִּכְתִיב בַּסֻּכֹּת בַּסֻּכֹּת. אִכָּא חָד בַּסֻכּוֹת דִּכְתִיב שְׁלִים. הָא חָד שְׁלִים לְאַחְזָאָה דְמַאן דְּיָתִיב בְּצִלָא דָא. יָתִיב בְּאִנּוּן יוֹמִין עִלָּאִין לְעֵלָּא. דְּקַיְימִין עַל הַאי תַּתָּאָה לְאַנְהָרָא לֵיהּ. לְחַפְיָא עֲלֵיהּ. וּלְאֲגָנָא עֲלֵיהּ בְּשַׁעְתָּא דְאִצְטְרִיךְ:

בָּךְ נָטְלִי יִשְׂרָאֵל פְּרִ֨י עֵ֤ץ הָדָר֙ כַּפֹּ֣ת תְּמָרִ֔ים וַעֲנַ֥ף עֵץ־עָבֹ֖ת וְעַרְבֵי־נָ֑חַל. וּבְהַנֵּי זִינִין אִתְחֲזוּן קַמֵּי קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא. בָּךְ מְתַקְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל כוּרְסְיָא לְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא מִתַּתָּא וּלְסַלְקָא לֵיהּ לְעֵלָּא בְּאִנּוּן זִינִין וּבְחֶדְוָה וּבְהִלּוּלָא וּבְהַקָּפָה. וּבְגִין דָּא סַלְקָא שְׁכִינְתָּא וְנַטְלָא בִרְכָאן וְחֶדְוָה בְּקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא. וְאִיהִי נַקְטָא נַפְשִׁין דְּעִנּוּגִין לְעֵלָּא. וְנַקְטָא כָּל בִּרְכָאן וְכָל קִדּוּשִׁין וְכָל עִנוּגִין. בָּר֖וּךְ יְהֹוָ֥ה לְ֝עוֹלָ֗ם אָ֘מֵ֥ן ׀ וְאָמֵֽן׃

שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ יוֹמָא טָבָא קַדִּישָׁא. שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ חַגָּא קַדִּישָׁא. שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ אוּשְׁפִּיזָא קַדִּישָׁא. אַנְתְּ הוּא מִקְרָא קוֹדֶשׁ. זַמִּין אַנְתְּ לְהַהוּא אֲתַר דְּאִקְרֵי קוֹדֶשׁ. לְאִתְעַטְּרָא בֵּיהּ וּלְאִשְׁתַּאֲבָא בֵּיהּ. וְתִתְקַדֵּשׁ וְיִשְׁתַּכַּח בָּךְ חֶדְוָתָא. הָא אַנְתְּ שָׁאִיב מֵהַהוּא עֲמִיקָא דַעֲמִיקְתָא. דְּנַחֲלִין וּמַבּוּעִין נַפְקִין מִנֵּיהּ. הָא יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאִקְרוּן קוֹדֶשׁ מְקַבְּלִין לָךְ בְּאַנְפִּין נְהִירִין. בְּחֶדְוָתָא בְּתֻשְׁבְּחָתָּא. מְזַמְּנִין לָךְ מְתַקְּנִין לָךְ סְעוּדָתָא יַקִּירָא. מְסַדְּרִין פָּתוֹרֵי מְתַקְּנֵי גַּרְמַיְהוּ בְּמָאנֵי יְקָר:

הָא בְּכָל שִׁבְעָה יוֹמִין דְּסֻכּוֹת, מָשְׁכִין יִשְׂרָאֵל לִשְׁכִינְתָּא בְּאִנּוּן עוֹבָדִין טָבִין דְּעָבְדִין וּמְקָרְבִין בַּהֲדָהּ. וּכְדֵין אִיהִי נָחֲתָא לְקָרְבָא בִּבְנָהָא וּלְמֶחֱדֵי לוֹן יוֹמָא חַד. דְּאִיהוּ יוֹמָא תְמִינָאָה דְּאִקְּרֵי עֲצֶרֶת. דָּא אִיהוּ יוֹמָא דְחֶדְוָה דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל בִּלְחוֹדַיְהוּ, וְלָא יִתְעָרְבוּן שְׁאַר עַמִּין בַּהֲדַיְהוּ. בֵּיהּ סִיהָרָא אִתְמַלֵּי בִּרְכָאן לְעֵלָּא כִּדְקָא יָאוּת. וְיִשְׂרָאֵל אַתְיַן וְיַנְקִין מִנָּהּ בִּלְחוֹדַיְהוּ. וְעַל דָּא כְּתִיב עֲצֶ֖רֶת תִּהְיֶ֣ה לָכֶ֑ם, כְּנִישׁוּ כָּל מָה דִּכְנִישׁוּ מֵאִנּוּן בִּרְכָאן עִלָּאִין. לָכֶם וְלֹא לִשְׁאַר מְמַנָּן. וְעַל הַאי יוֹמָא כְּתִיב דּוֹדִ֥י לִי֙ וַאֲנִ֣י ל֔וֹ, דְּלָא אִתְעֲרַב אוֹחֲרָא בַּהֲדָן. בְּהַאי יוֹמָא מַלְכָּא קַדִּישָׁא יָהִיב לָן כָּל צָרְכָנָא דְּנִשְׁאַל מִנֵּיהּ. זַכָּאָה הַאי יוֹמָא וְזַכָּאִין אִנּוּן יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאַחְסִינוּ דָּא. אַשְׁרֵ֣י הָ֭עָם שֶׁכָּ֣כָה לּ֑וֹ אַֽשְׁרֵ֥י הָ֝עָ֗ם שֱׁיְהֹוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃

שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ יוֹמָא טָבָא קַדִּישָׁא. שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ חַגָּא קַדִּישָׁא. שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ אוּשְׁפִּיזָא קַדִּישָׁא. אַנְתְּ הוּא מִקְרָא קוֹדֶשׁ. זַמִּין אַנְתְּ לְהַהוּא אֲתַר דְּאִקְרֵי קוֹדֶשׁ. לְאִתְעַטְּרָא בֵּיהּ וּלְאִשְׁתַּאֲבָא בֵּיהּ. וְתִתְקַדַּשׁ וְיִשְׁתַּכַּח בָּךְ חֶדְוָתָא. הָא אַנְתְּ שָׁאִיב מֵהַהוּא עֲמִיקָא דַעֲמִיקָתָא. דְּנַחֲלִין וּמַבּוּעִין נַפְקִין מִנֵּיהּ. הָא יִשְׂרָאֵל דְּאִתְקְרוּן קוֹדֶשׁ מְקַבְּלִין לָךְ בְּאַנְפִּין נְהִירִין. בְּחֶדְוָתָא וּבְתֻשְׁבַּחְתָּא. מְזַמְּנִין לָךְ מְתַקְּנִין לָךְ סְעוּדָתָא יְקִּירָא. מְסַדְּרִין פָּתוֹרֵי. מְתַקְּנֵי גַּרְמַיְהוּ בְּמָאנֵי יְקָר. חֲדָאן וּמְשַׁבְּחִין שְׁבָחָא לְקֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא:

שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ יוֹמָא דְחַג הַשָּׁבוּעוֹת. שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ יוֹמָא טָבָא דְאוֹרַיְתָא. אַנְתְּ הוּא קִשּׁוּרָא דִמְהֵימְנוּתָא קִשּׁוּרָא דְכֹלָּא. בָּךְ אִשְׁתְּמוֹדְעָא מְהֵימְנוּתָא וְקִשּׁוּרָא שְׁלֵימָא וְיִחוּדָא עִלָּאָה קַדִּישָׁא. אַנְתְּ הוּא קִשּׁוּרָא דְכֹלָּא וְאֶמְצָעִיתָא דְכֹלָּא דְיָתַבְתְּ בֵּין פֶּסַח וְסֻכּוֹת. בָּךְ הוּא שְׁבָחָא דְאוֹרַיְתָא. בָּךְ הוּא חֶדְוָתָא דְאוֹרַיְתָא. בָּךְ הוּא שְׁבָחָא דִמְהֵימְנוּתָא וְקִשּׁוּרָא דְכֹלָּא דְּעֵלָּא וְתַתָּא. בָּךְ הוּא חֶדְוָתָא דְעִלָּאֵי וְתַתָּאֵי וְחֶדְוָתָא דְסִיהֲרָא. בָּךְ אִתְיְהִיבַת אוֹרַיְתָא. בָּךְ אִתְעַטְּרַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּעַטְרִין עִלָּאִין:

שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ יוֹמָא טָבָא דַעֲצֶרֶת. שְׁלָמָא עֲלָךְ יוֹמָא טָבָא דְשָׁבוּעוֹת. בָּךְ עָאלוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְרָזָא דְחַמְשִׁין יוֹמִין דְּאִנּוּן שִׁבְעָה שָׁבוּעוֹת. בָּךְ אִתְכְּנָשׁוּ כָּל נְהוֹרִין לְאֵשֶׁת חַיִל. בָּךְ אִתְיְהִיבוּ תְּרֵין לוּחִין דְּאוֹרַיְתָא מִסִּטְרָא דְאִילָנָא דְחַיֵּי. בָּךְ קְרִיבוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל לְטוּרָא דְסִינָי. בָּךְ נָחַת הַהוּא טַלָּא עִלָּאָה בִּשְׁלִימוּ וְאִתְדַּכּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאִתְפַּסְּקַת זוֹהֲמָתָן מִנַּיְהוּ. בָּךְ אִתְחַבָּרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּמַלְכָּא קַדִּישָׁא וּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא קַדִּישָׁא וְקַבִּילוּ אוֹרַיְתָא. בָּךְ יַרְתִין עַמָּא קַדִּישָׁא יְרוּתָא קַדִּישָׁא לְהוּ וְלִבְנַיְהוּ בִּתְרֵין עָלְמִין. בָּךְ אִתְעַטְּרַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל עַל עַמָּא קַדִּישָׁא. בָּךְ מְתַקְנִין יִשְׂרָאֵל תַּכְשִׁיטֵי כַּלָּה בְּגִין דְּתִשְׁתַּכָּח בְּתַכְשִׁיטָהָא וְתִקּוּנָהָא לְגַבֵּי מַלְכָּא קַדִּישָׁא כִּדְקָא יָאוּת. בָּר֖וּךְ יְהֹוָ֥ה לְ֝עוֹלָ֗ם אָ֘מֵ֥ן ׀ וְאָמֵֽן׃

אוֹרַיְתָא אוֹרַיְתָא, נְהִירוּ דְּכָל-עַלְמִין, כַּמָּה יַמִּין, וּנְחָלִין, וּמְקוֹרִין, וּמַבּוּעִין, מִתְפַּשְּׁטִין מִנָּךְ לְכָל-סִטְרָא. מִנָּךְ כֹּלָּא, עֲלָךְ קַיְמֵי עִלָּאִין וְתַתָּאִין, נְהִירוּ עִלָּאָה וַדַּאי מִנָּךְ נַפְקֵי.

אוֹרַיְתָא אוֹרַיְתָא, מָה-אֵימָא לְגַבָּךְ, אַיֶּלֶת אַהָבִים אַנְתְּ, וְיַעֲלַת חֵן. עֵלָּא וְתַתָּא רַחֲמִין דִּילָךְ. מַאן יִזְכֵּי לְיַנְקָא מִנָּךְ כְּדְקָא יָאוֹת. אַנְתְּ שַׁעֲשׁוּעִים דְּמָרָךְ, מַאן יָכִיל לְגַלָּאָה, וּלְמֵימָר סִתְרִין וּגְנִיזִין דִּילָךְ.

אוֹרַיְתָא אוֹרַיְתָא, עַלָךְ כְּתִיב: וָֽאֶהְיֶ֥ה אֶצְל֗וֹ אָ֫מ֥וֹן וָֽאֶהְיֶ֣ה שַׁ֭עֲשֻׁעִים י֤וֹם ׀ י֑וֹם. בָּךְ אִתְבְּנֵי עַלְמָא וְאִשְׁתַּכְלַל וְכָל־דְּאִשְׁתַּדַּל בָּךְ שַׁכְלִיל עַלְמִין וְקִיֵּם לוֹן, וְקִיֵּם כָּל־עוֹבָדָא וְעוֹבָדָא עַל תִּקּוּנֵהּ כִּדְקָא יָאוֹת, וְכָל־מַאן דְּאִשְׁתַּדַּל בָּךְ וְאִתְאַחִיד בָּךְ אִתְאַחִיד בְּאִילָנָא דְחַיֵּי.

אוֹרַיְתָא אוֹרַיְתָא, עֲלָךְ כְּתִיב: יְקָ֣רָה הִ֭יא מִפְּנִינִ֑ים. כַּמָּה גְנִיזִין טְמִירִין אִית בָּךְ. כַּמָּה פְלִיאָן נַפְקִין מִנָּךְ. כָּל־אִנּוּן מִלִּין עִלָּאִין דְּאִתְגַּלְיָן וּדְלָא אִתְגַּלְיָן בָּךְ אִנּוּן. כָּל־מִלִּין דִּלְעֵלָּא וּלְתַתָּא וְכָל־מִלִּין דְּעַלְמָא דְאָתֵי בָּךְ אִנּוּן. מַאן יָכִיל לְמֵיקַם עַל מִלִּין דִּילָךְ, הָדָא הוּא דִכְתִיב: מִ֗י יְ֭מַלֵּל גְּבוּר֣וֹת יְהֹוָ֑ה.

אוֹרַיְתָא אוֹרַיְתָא, כַּמָּה טָבִין אִנּוּן אָרְחִין וּשְׁבִילִין דִּילָךְ, דְּהָא בְּכָל־מִלָּה וּמִלָּה דִילָךְ אִית בַּהּ כַּמָּה עֵיטִין כַּמָּה טָבִין לִבְנֵי נְשָׁא. וְאִית בְּהוֹן כַּמָּה מַרְגְּלָאן דְּקָא מַנְהִירִין לְכָל־סְטַר. וְלֵית מִלָּה בָךְ דְּלֵית בַּהּ כַּמָּה בוֹצִינִין מְנַהֲרָן לְכָל־סְטַר.

אוֹרַיְתָא אוֹרַיְתָא, כַּמָּה חֲבִיבִין אִנּוּן מִלִּין דִּילָךְ. מָה אִילָנָא אִית בֵּהּ שָׁרָשִׁין, וְאִית בֵּהּ קְלִפִּין, וְאִית בֵּהּ מוֹחָא, וְאִית בֵּהּ עַנְפִין, וְאִית בֵּהּ טַרְפִּין, וְאִית בֵּהּ פִּרְחִין, וְאִית בֵּהּ אֵיבָא, אוּף הָכִי אִנּוּן מִלִּין דִּילָךְ, אִית בְּהוּ פְּשָׁטֵי דִקְרָאֵי, דְּרָשָׁא וְרֶמֶז דְּקָא רָמִיז חָכְמְתָא, גֵּמַטְרִיָּאוֹת, רָזִין טְמִירִין רָזִין סְתִימִין, אִלֵּין עַל אִלֵּין, כָּשֵׁר וּפָסוּל, טָמֵא וְטָהוֹר, אָסוּר וּמֻתָּר, חַיָּב וְזַכַּאי. וּמִכָּאן וּלְהָלְאָה מִתְפַּשְּׁטָאן עַנְפִין לְכָל־סְטַר. רְחָבָה אַנְתְּ מִנִּי יָם, לֵית בָּךְ קֵץ וְתַכְלִית.

אוֹרַיְתָא אוֹרַיְתָא, אוֹרַיְתָא עִלָּאָה, אוֹרַיְתָא דִקְשֹׁט, כַּמָּה חֲבִיבָה אַנְתְּ קַמֵּי קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא. חֲבִיבָה אַנְתְּ לְעֵלָּא וַחֲבִיבָה אַנְתְּ לְתַתָּא. כָּל־שְׁבִילִין דִּילָךְ כֻּלְהוֹן שְׁלִים, שְׁלִים לְעֵלָּא שְׁלִים לְתַתָּא, שְׁלִים בְּעַלְמָא דֵין שְׁלִים בְּעַלְמָא דְאָתֵי.

אוֹרַיְתָא אוֹרַיְתָא, הָא אַהֲבָה וְרִשְׁפִּין דְּשַׁלְהוּבָא דְלִבָּא אַבַּתְרָךְ. יְהֵא רַעֲוָא, תִּהְיִי אַנְתְּ חֲקוּקָה בְלִבָּן. הַדְרָךְ עֲלָן אוֹרַיְתָא קַדִּישְׁתָּא, וְהַדְרָן עֲלָךְ אוֹרַיְתָא קַדִּישְׁתָּא, דַּעְתָּךְ עֲלָן אוֹרַיְתָא קַדִּישְׁתָּא, וְדַעְתָּן עֲלָךְ אוֹרַיְתָא קַדִּישְׁתָּא, לָא נִתְנְשֵׁי מִנָּךְ וְלָא תִתְנְשִׁי מִנָּן, לָא בְעַלְמָא דֵין וְלָא בְעַלְמָא דְאָתִי. בְּגִין זְכוּתָא דְמֹשֶׁה רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, וְכָל־זַכָּאִין צַדִּיקִין וַחֲסִידִין דִּקְשׁוֹט, וּבְגִין מַלְאֲכָא (ויופיא"ל) רַב מְמַנָּא, וְחַמְשִׁין וּתְלָת רְתִיכִין דִּתְחוֹת יְדֵהּ דְּמַתְנֵי בְּשִׁמּוּשָׁא דְאוֹרַיְתָא, כָּל־חַד וְחַד עַל אַתְרֵהּ, וְסַלְקִין לְכָל־פָּרָשָׁתָא וּפָרָשָׁתָא לְאִתְעַטְּרָא קַמֵּי קֻדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא לְאִתְיַחֲדָא לְעֵלָּא לְעֵלָּא.

Peace to you, good and holy day. Peace to you, holy festival. Peace to you, holy guest. You are a holy convocation. You are prepared for that place that is called holy, to be crowned in it and to draw from it, and to be sanctified, and joy is found in you. Behold, you draw from that depth of depths from which streams and springs go forth. Behold, Israel, who are called holy, receive you with shining faces, with joy and with praise; they invite you and prepare a precious meal for you; they set out the tables and adorn themselves in precious garments, rejoicing and offering praise to the Holy One, blessed be He.

Festival of Sukkot, how dear and precious you are. Although this month is covered and not revealed, in you it is revealed, in the joy of the moon. In you the moon is completed and illumined by the supernal Mother, and she stands to give light to those below from within the light above.

In you the Holy One, blessed be He, spreads His wings over Israel and rejoices with them. In you the right side awakens above, so that the moon may be bound to it and its face shine as is proper. In you Israel go out with signs, marked by the holy King, for they are victorious in judgment. For in you Israel go out with the King’s mark, with the praise of rejoicing; they enter the sukkot and take the etrog in the left hand and the lulav in the right. And the upper and lower beings see Israel marked with the marks of the holy King, for they take the signs of faith, the seal of the supernal King.

In you it is written, “You shall dwell in booths for seven days,” to show that Israel sit in the mystery of faith without any fear at all, for the accuser is separated from them, and all the supernal accusers return to loving Israel. In you the upper and lower beings will know, and the glory of the Holy One, blessed be He, is raised above and below as is fitting. And all the supernal hosts open and say: “And who is like Your people Israel, a unique nation on the earth?”

In you Israel dwell in the shade of faith, and therefore they inherit freedom for themselves and their children forever, and are blessed with the supernal blessing. In you we dwell in the shade of faith, and therefore the Shechinah spreads her wings over us from above. In you we invite the holy guests, who are Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David. And these righteous ones, the holy guests, make their dwellings with us in this shade of faith. And Abraham, the holy father, recites over us: “Then you shall delight in Hashem, and I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth, and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father, for the mouth of Hashem has spoken.” And Isaac, the holy father, recites over us: “His seed shall be mighty in the land; the generation of the upright shall be blessed. Wealth and riches are in his house, and his righteousness endures forever.” And Jacob, the holy father, recites over us: “Then your light shall break forth like the dawn, and your healing shall spring up speedily.” And Moses the faithful shepherd, and Aaron the great and holy kohen, and Joseph the holy righteous one, recite over us: “And Hashem will guide you always, and satisfy your soul in drought, and strengthen your bones; and you shall be like a watered garden, like a spring of water whose waters do not fail. And those from you shall build the ancient ruins; you shall raise up the foundations of many generations, and you shall be called the repairer of the breach, the restorer of paths to dwell in.” And David, the holy king Messiah, who is appointed over all the weapons of the world, recites over us: “No weapon formed against you shall prosper, and every tongue that rises against you in judgment you shall condemn. This is the heritage of the servants of Hashem, and their righteousness is from Me, says Hashem.”

Festival of Sukkot, how very dear and precious you are. In you we perform the commandment of the sukkah, which alludes to the supernal Mother, who shelters over us as a mother over her children; and in you we invite to us the seven exalted holy guests, who correspond to the seven sefirot. For on account of the seven sefirot Scripture says: “For I made the children of Israel dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt”—in the seven clouds of glory. A sukkah spelled fully, with the letter vav, is in the mystery of the two Names: the two cherubim who cover with their wings over the ark-cover, their faces toward one another. And it is written, “And there shall be a booth for shade by day,” for we require schach; and schach is made for a shade of which it is said, “He who dwells in the shelter of the Most High abides in the shadow of the Almighty”—not the shade of an ordinary booth that protects the body from the sun, but a shade that protects the soul, as it is written: “In his shade I delighted and sat.”

Festival of Sukkot, how dear and precious you are. In you we perform the commandment of taking the lulav, which resembles the spine, in which there are eighteen shakings of the lulav. These correspond to the eighteen blessings of the prayer, and to the eighteen mentions [of the Name] in the psalm “Render to Hashem, O sons of the mighty,” and to the eighteen mentions in the Shema. And the shaking toward the six directions is counted as six, and three shakings toward each direction are “chai” (eighteen). The lulav, which is the righteous one, we take in the right hand. Behold, it includes six species: the three myrtles are Greatness, Might, and Splendor, which resemble the three colors of the eye; further, the two willow branches are Eternity and Majesty, which resemble the two lips; and the lulav, which is Foundation, resembles the spine, in which is the support of all the bones, and of it King David said: “All my bones shall say: Hashem, who is like You?” And in the left hand we take the etrog, Kingship, which resembles the heart, in which are the thoughts. For this reason the etrog, which resembles the heart, was instituted to be in the left hand. But the lulav is in the right hand, which is the mystery of Kindness, the right arm.

Festival of Sukkot, how dear and precious you are. In you Israel go out with signs, marked from the house of the King. These are the species that are attached to the Holy Name; these are the signs of faith, the seal of the supernal King. Of them it is said: “Everyone who is called by My Name, whom I created for My glory, whom I formed, whom I also made.” “Everyone who is called by My Name”: this is “the fruit of a goodly tree.” “Whom I created for My glory”: this is “branches of palm trees.” “Whom I formed”: this is “a bough of a leafy tree.” “Whom I also made”: this is “willows of the brook.”

In you it is written: “And you shall take for yourselves on the first day.” This is that which comes forth first to draw from the sources of the flowing waters, and we desire to draw it down. For the Day of Atonement brings everything out to freedom; and on this day the supernal Matron, who is the Jubilee that brought us out to freedom, crowns the King with His crowns. And we know that flowing waters dwell with her and we are ready to drink. Therefore we call it “the first day.”

Furthermore, “And you shall take for yourselves on the first day”: on this day Abraham is the beginning of everything. Whether by the clouds of glory, he is the beginning; whether by water, he is the beginning; for Abraham began to dig wells of water. “The fruit of a goodly tree” is the well of Isaac, for Isaac returned it to the Holy One, blessed be He, and called it “hadar,” the fruit of this “goodly tree.” “Branches of palm trees,” as it is written, “The righteous flourishes like the palm tree”; and no separation is found between them. Therefore it is not written “and branches” but “branches,” since it does not rise without this one. And through this one this well is filled, a well of supernal flowing waters; it was filled first, and from it the well is filled, until it flows for all. “And a bough of a leafy tree”: this is the branch of the great tree, which became strong and took root in its roots and became the supreme tree over all, holding on every side—a branch which is a leafy tree, a tree that holds the fathers. For from this the foundation of the world takes, and the earth is filled in the well; this is the world, the land of watering. “And willows of the brook” are two: two streams of water gathered in them for the earth, for the righteous one.

Festival of Sukkot, how very dear and precious you are. In you it is written, “You shall dwell in booths for seven days”: this is the mystery of faith, seven days from the upper world to the lower, all of which stand in their station to give light to this sukkah, which is the sukkah of David, the sukkah of peace. And the holy people sit beneath its shade in the mystery of faith; and whoever sits in this shade sits in those upper days. Therefore, although it is written “in booths, in booths,” there is one “sukkot” written in full. This is one full spelling, to show that whoever sits in this shade sits in those upper days above, which stand over this lower one to give it light, to cover over it, and to protect it at the time of need.

In you Israel take the fruit of a goodly tree, branches of palm trees, a bough of a leafy tree, and willows of the brook, and with these species they appear before the Holy One, blessed be He. In you Israel prepare a throne for the Holy One, blessed be He, from below, and raise it up to Him above with these species, with joy, with rejoicing, and with the circuit. And therefore the Shechinah rises and takes blessings and joy from the Holy One, blessed be He; and she takes souls of delights above, and takes all blessings, all holiness, and all delights. Blessed is Hashem forever. Amen and Amen.

Peace to you, good and holy day. Peace to you, holy festival. Peace to you, holy guest. You are a holy convocation. You are prepared for that place that is called holy, to be crowned in it and to draw from it, and to be sanctified, and joy is found in you. Behold, you draw from that depth of depths from which streams and springs go forth. Behold, Israel, who are called holy, receive you with shining faces, with joy and with praise; they invite you and prepare a precious meal for you; they set out the tables and adorn themselves in precious garments.

Throughout all seven days of Sukkot, Israel draw the Shechinah to them by the good deeds they do and by bringing themselves near to her. And then she descends to be near her children and to rejoice with them for one day, the eighth day, which is called Atzeret. This is the day of Israel’s joy alone, and the other nations do not mingle with them. On it the moon is filled with blessings above, as is fitting, and Israel come and nurse from her alone. Therefore it is written, “It shall be an Atzeret for you”: gather all that you have gathered of those supernal blessings, for you and not for the other appointed powers. Of this day it is written, “My beloved is mine and I am his,” for no other is mingled with us. On this day the holy King gives us everything we need to ask of Him. Happy is this day, and happy is Israel, who inherit it. “Happy is the people who have it so; happy is the people whose God is Hashem.”

Peace to you, good and holy day. Peace to you, holy festival. Peace to you, holy guest. You are a holy convocation. You are prepared for that place that is called holy, to be crowned in it and to draw from it, and to be sanctified, and joy is found in you. Behold, you draw from that depth of depths from which streams and springs go forth. Behold, Israel, who are called holy, receive you with shining faces, with joy and with praise; they invite you and prepare a precious meal for you; they set out the tables and adorn themselves in precious garments, rejoicing and offering praise to the Holy One, blessed be He.

Peace to you, day of the Festival of Shavuot. Peace to you, good day of the Torah. You are the knot of faith, the knot of all. In you faith is known, and the complete knot and the supreme holy unity. You are the knot of all and the middle of all, who sit between Pesach and Sukkot. In you is the praise of the Torah. In you is the joy of the Torah. In you is the praise of faith and the knot of all, above and below. In you is the joy of the upper and lower beings, and the joy of the moon. In you the Torah was given. In you the Assembly of Israel was crowned with supernal crowns.

Peace to you, good day of Atzeret. Peace to you, good day of Shavuot. In you Israel entered the mystery of the fifty days, which are seven weeks. In you all the lights gathered to the woman of valor. In you the two tablets of the Torah were given, from the side of the Tree of Life. In you Israel drew near to Mount Sinai. In you that supernal dew descended in perfection, and Israel were purified and their impurity ceased from them. In you Israel were joined with the holy King and the holy Matron, and received the Torah. In you the holy people inherit a holy inheritance, for themselves and their children, in two worlds. In you the Assembly of Israel was crowned over the holy people. In you Israel prepare the ornaments of the bride, so that she may be found, with her ornaments and her adornments, before the holy King as is fitting. Blessed is Hashem forever. Amen and Amen.

Torah, Torah, light of all the worlds! How many streams, rivers, sources, and springs spread out from you in every direction. From you comes everything; upon you the upper and lower worlds stand; surely the supernal light comes forth from you.

Torah, Torah, how like a mother you are to those who cling to you, a loving doe and a graceful gazelle. Those above and below love you. Who is worthy to nurse from you as is fitting? You are the delight of your Master; who can reveal and speak of your hidden and treasured secrets?

Torah, Torah, of you it is written: “Then I was beside Him as a nursling, and I was His delight day by day.” Through you the world was built and perfected, and whoever labors in you perfects the worlds and sustains them, and sustains every deed in its proper arrangement; and whoever labors in you and clings to you clings to the Tree of Life.

Torah, Torah, of you it is written: “She is more precious than rubies.” How many hidden treasures are in you! How many wonders come forth from you! All those supernal words, revealed and not revealed, are in you. All the words above and below and all the words of the world to come are in you. Who can stand upon your words? This is what is written: “Who can utter the mighty acts of Hashem?”

Torah, Torah, how good are your paths and ways, for in each and every word of yours there are many counsels, many good things for people; and in them are many pearls that shine in every direction. And there is no word in you in which there are not many lamps that shine in every direction.

Torah, Torah, how dear are your words. Just as a tree has roots, and bark, and pith, and branches, and leaves, and flowers, and fruit, so too are your words: they contain the plain meaning of the verses, homiletic interpretation, and allusion that hints at wisdom, gematria, hidden secrets and concealed secrets, one upon another; fit and unfit, impure and pure, forbidden and permitted, guilty and innocent. And from here onward branches spread in every direction. You are wider than the sea; in you there is no end or limit.

Torah, Torah, supernal Torah, Torah of truth, how dear you are before the Holy One, blessed be He. You are dear above and you are dear below. All your paths are perfect: perfect above, perfect below, perfect in this world, perfect in the world to come.

Torah, Torah, behold the love and the flaming sparks of the fire of the heart for you. May it be His will that you be engraved on our hearts. May you return to us, holy Torah, and may we return to you, holy Torah; may your attention be on us, holy Torah, and our attention on you, holy Torah. May we not forget you and may you not forget us, neither in this world nor in the world to come. For the sake of the merit of Moses the faithful shepherd, and of all the righteous, pious, and true ones, and for the sake of the angel (Yofiel), the great appointee, and the fifty-three chariots under his hand, who are appointed over the service of the Torah, each one in his place, and who ascend with each and every parashah to be crowned before the Holy One, blessed be He, to be united above, above.

segs.text: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה יְהֹוָה, אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ מֶֽלֶךְ הָעוֹלָם, בּוֹרֵא פְּרִי הַגֶּֽפֶן:

A psalm of David. Hashem is my shepherd; I shall not want. He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside still waters. He restores my soul; He guides me in paths of righteousness for His Name’s sake. Even when I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me. You prepare a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You have anointed my head with oil; my cup overflows. Surely goodness and kindness will pursue me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the House of Hashem for length of days.

If you restrain your foot on account of the Sabbath, from doing your pleasure on My holy day, and call the Sabbath a delight, the holy day of Hashem honored, and honor it by not doing your usual ways, not pursuing your own affairs or speaking words—then you shall delight in Hashem, and I will make you ride upon the heights of the earth, and feed you with the inheritance of Jacob your father, for the mouth of Hashem has spoken.

The children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, observing the Sabbath throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant. It is a sign between Me and the children of Israel forever, for in six days Hashem made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased from work and rested.

“And on the day of your gladness, and on your festivals, and on your new moons, you shall blow the trumpets over your burnt offerings and over your peace offerings; and they shall be a remembrance for you before your God. I am Hashem your God.”
“These are the appointed times of Hashem, holy convocations, which you shall proclaim in their appointed times.” And Moses declared the appointed times of Hashem to the children of Israel.

Three times a year all your males shall appear before Hashem your God in the place that He will choose: on the Festival of Matzot, on the Festival of Shavuot, and on the Festival of Sukkot. They shall not appear before Hashem empty-handed; each man with the gift of his hand, according to the blessing of Hashem your God that He has given you.
Therefore Hashem blessed the Sabbath day and sanctified it.
With your permission, my masters. To life!
Blessed are You, Hashem our God, King of the universe, Who creates the fruit of the vine.

parts.text: אֵל מִמִּצְרַֽיִם גְּאָלָֽנוּ. דִּבְּרוֹת קָדְשׁוֹ הִשְׁמִיעָֽנוּ. עֲנָנֵי כָבוֹד הִקִּיפָֽנוּ. לְאַרְבַּע רוּחוֹת מַֽטָּה וּמָֽעְלָה:
<small>סֻכָּה וְלוּלָב לְעַם סְגֻלָּה. יַֽחַד יָרֹֽנּוּ יִשְׂאוּ תְהִלָּה:</small>
נֹֽעַם דְּרָכָיו לָֽנוּ הוֹדִֽיעַ. מִזִּיו הֲדָרוֹ לָֽנוּ הוֹפִֽיעַ. דַּעַת יוֹם לְיוֹם אֹמֶר יַבִּֽיעַ. דַּעַת יְחַוֶּה לַֽיְלָה לְלָֽיְלָה:
<small>סֻכָּה וְלוּלָב לְעַם סְגֻלָּה. יַֽחַד יָרֹֽנּוּ יִשְׂאוּ תְהִלָּה:</small>
יִשְׂמַח יִשְׂרָאַל בְּצֵל סֻכָּתוֹ. יִסְתּוֹפֵף יֶחֱסֶה תַּֽחַת אֶבְרָתוֹ. הַשֵּׁם כִּכְתָבוֹ וְכִקְרִיאָתוֹ. כְּמִסְפַּר סֻכָּה מִסְפָּרוֹ עָלָה:
<small>סֻכָּה וְלוּלָב לְעַם סְגֻלָּה. יַֽחַד יָרֹֽנּוּ יִשְׂאוּ תְהִלָּה:</small>
מֶה עָצְמוּ רָזֵי לוּלָב וּמִינָיו. וְלִי מַה יָּקְרוּ מְאֹד עִנְיָנָיו. אַשְׁרֵי טְהָר-לֵב הַשָּׂם רַעְיוֹנָיו. לְסוֹד מִצְוָתוֹ הַמְּעֻלָּה:
<small>סֻכָּה וְלוּלָב לְעַם סְגֻלָּה. יַֽחַד יָרֹֽנּוּ יִשְׂאוּ תְהִלָּה:</small>
שֵׁם בֶּן אַרְבַּע בַּלּוּלָב חוֹנֶה. בְּמִילּוּי הֵהִי"ן בִּפְרָטָיו תִּמְנֶה. נֹֽכַח הַלּוּלָב לַשִּׁדְרָה תִפְנֶה. סְבִיבָיו מִינָיו גֹּרֶן עֲגֻלָּה:
<small>סֻכָּה וְלוּלָב לְעַם סְגֻלָּה. יַֽחַד יָרֹֽנּוּ יִשְׂאוּ תְהִלָּה:</small>
הֶהָדָס רוֹמֵז לִשְׁלֹשָׁה אָבוֹת. מֹשֶׁה אַהֲרֹן בַּדֵּי עֲרָבוֹת. יוֹסֵף לַלּוּלָב חֶמְדַּת לְבָבוֹת. דָּוִד לָאֶתְרוֹג כַּלָּה כְּלוּלָה:
<small>סֻכָּה וְלוּלָב לְעַם סְגֻלָּה. יַֽחַד יָרֹֽנּוּ יִשְׂאוּ תְהִלָּה:</small>
חוֹתָם תְּעוּדָה תַּתִּיר לְבִנְךָ. זֶבֶד טוֹב תִּזְבֹּד לְעַם לְךָ. קוֹרֵא וּמְיַחֵל לִישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ. יִתְקַדַּשׁ שִׁמְךָ בְּפִֽינוּ סֶֽלָה:

יָהּ אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִד תָּקִים. בִּזְכוּת שִׁבְעַת הַצַּדִּיקִים:

parts.text: בִּזְכוּת אַבְרָהָם אֶזְרַח תְּמִימֶֽךָ. מְשֹׁךְ חַסְדָּךְ לְעַמֶּֽךָ. וְנָא לְמַעַן שְׁמֶֽךָ. אַל נָא תָּשֵׁב אוֹתָם רֵקִים:
<small>יָהּ אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִד תָּקִים. בִּזְכוּת שִׁבְעַת הַצַּדִּיקִים:</small>
בִּזְכוּת יִצְחָק עֲקֵדֶֽךָ. בָּרֵךְ דּוֹרְשֵׁי יְחוּדֶֽךָ. וְנָא גְבוּרוֹת יָדֶֽיךָ. בְּחַסְדָּךְ יִהְיוּ נִמְתָּקִים:
<small>יָהּ אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִד תָּקִים. בִּזְכוּת שִׁבְעַת הַצַּדִּיקִים:</small>
בִּזְכוּת יַעֲקֹב אִישׁ תָּמִים. הוּא נֶֽגֶד קַו הָרַחֲמִים. תִּבְנֶה בֵיתְךָ בֵּית עוֹלָמִים. קַיָּם בִּשְׁמֵי שְׁחָקִים:
<small>יָהּ אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִד תָּקִים. בִּזְכוּת שִׁבְעַת הַצַּדִּיקִים:</small>
בִּזְכוּת מֹשֶׁה רַעְיָה מְהֵימְנָא. זָכָה לְפָנִים שֶׁל בִּינָה. חֽוּשָׁה תֵּן לָֽנוּ חֲנִינָה. וּפְדֵם עַם לְךָ שׁוֹקְקִים:
<small>יָהּ אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִד תָּקִים. בִּזְכוּת שִׁבְעַת הַצַּדִּיקִים:</small>
בִּזְכוּת הַכֹּהֵן אַהֲרֹן. בַּטֵּל כָּל-הָאַף וַחֲרוֹן. וְעַמָּךְ תָּמִיד רוֹן יָרוֹן. וּבִשְׁמָךְ יִהְיוּ דְבוּקִים:
<small>יָהּ אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִד תָּקִים. בִּזְכוּת שִׁבְעַת הַצַּדִּיקִים:</small>
בִּזְכוּת יוֹסֵף צַדִּיקֶֽךָ. אֲשֶׁר שָׁמַר בְּרִיתֶֽךָ. גַּלֵּה כְבוֹד מַלְכוּתֶֽךָ. קַבֵּץ נִדָּחִים וּרְחוֹקִים:
<small>יָהּ אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִד תָּקִים. בִּזְכוּת שִׁבְעַת הַצַּדִּיקִים:</small>
בִּזְכוּת דָּוִד יְדִידֶֽךָ. בְּנֵה מִשְׁכַּן כְּבוֹדֶֽךָ. וְאַמֵּץ עַם נְדוּדֶֽךָ. לַמְּדֵם תּוֹרָה וְחֻקִּים:
<small>יָהּ אֶת סֻכַּת דָּוִד תָּקִים. בִּזְכוּת שִׁבְעַת הַצַּדִּיקִים:</small>

segs.text: Sukkah and lulav, a treasured gift for the people; together we will sing and lift up praise.

He redeemed us from Egypt; He let us hear His holy utterances; the clouds of glory encircled us, to the four directions, below and above. Sukkah and lulav, a treasured gift for the people; together we will sing and lift up praise.

He made known to us the pleasantness of His ways; He revealed to us the radiance of His glory. “Day to day pours forth speech of knowledge,” the knowledge of Hashem, “night to night.” Sukkah and lulav, a treasured gift for the people; together we will sing and lift up praise.

Israel will rejoice in the shade of its sukkah; it will huddle and take refuge under His wing. The Name as it is written and as it is read: its numerical value rises to equal that of “sukkah.” Sukkah and lulav, a treasured gift for the people; together we will sing and lift up praise.

How vast are the secrets of the lulav and its species, and to me how precious are their matters. Happy is the pure of heart, whose thoughts are on the Name, on the secret of its commandment, the supreme ascent. Sukkah and lulav, a treasured gift for the people; together we will sing and lift up praise.

The four-letter Name rests in the lulav; in the filling of the letters Heh it is counted in its details. Facing the lulav, it turns toward the spine; around it, its species, in a circle like a threshing floor. Sukkah and lulav, a treasured gift for the people; together we will sing and lift up praise.

The myrtle alludes to the three fathers; Moses and Aaron are the willow branches; Joseph is the lulav, the desire of hearts; David is the etrog, the bride in full beauty. Sukkah and lulav, a treasured gift for the people; together we will sing and lift up praise.

Loosen the sealed testimony for Your child; give a good gift to the people who are Yours; the one who calls out and waits for Your salvation—may Your Name be sanctified in our mouths, Selah. Sukkah and lulav, a treasured gift for the people; together we will sing and lift up praise.
O Yah, raise up the fallen sukkah of David, in the merit of the seven righteous.

In the merit of Abraham, Your faithful and perfect one: draw out Your kindness to Your people, and please, for Your Name’s sake, do not send them back empty. O Yah, raise up the fallen sukkah of David, in the merit of the seven righteous.

In the merit of Isaac, Your bound one: bless those who seek Your unity, and please, may the severities of Your hands be sweetened by Your kindness. O Yah, raise up the fallen sukkah of David, in the merit of the seven righteous.

In the merit of Jacob, the perfect man, who is aligned with the line of mercy: rebuild Your house, an everlasting house, established in the heights of heaven. O Yah, raise up the fallen sukkah of David, in the merit of the seven righteous.

In the merit of Moses, the faithful shepherd, who merited the face of Understanding: hasten, grant us grace, and redeem Your people who long for You. O Yah, raise up the fallen sukkah of David, in the merit of the seven righteous.

In the merit of Aaron the kohen: cancel all anger and wrath, and Your people will always sing out in joy, clinging to Your Name. O Yah, raise up the fallen sukkah of David, in the merit of the seven righteous.

In the merit of Joseph, Your righteous one, who guarded Your covenant: reveal the glory of Your kingship; gather the dispersed and those who are far away. O Yah, raise up the fallen sukkah of David, in the merit of the seven righteous.

In the merit of David, Your beloved: build the dwelling of Your glory, strengthen Your wandering people, and teach them Torah and statutes. O Yah, raise up the fallen sukkah of David, in the merit of the seven righteous.
